intro: The Brewers are running the show in the World Series, dropping the Rays to 0-2 after another stunning win to put Milwaukee one step closer to a championship. Meanwhile, UCF just torched the college football landscape by knocking off No. 2 BYU in double overtime, and Week 8 is an absolute mess.

stories.headline: Brewers Stun Rays Again to Go Up 2-0 in the World Series
stories.body: Milwaukee erased a 4-0 deficit in Game 2, with Sal Frelick's sixth-inning homer and rookie Cooper Pratt's go-ahead RBI single sealing a 5-4 win — the Brewers' second four-run comeback of this postseason. The Series shifts to Tampa Bay, where the Rays desperately need to figure out how to stop digging their own graves with defensive miscues and baserunning blunders.

stories.headline: William Contreras Is Quietly Running the Show for Milwaukee
stories.body: Contreras has four hits, two caught-stealing in Game 1, and a crucial tag at home in Game 2 — he's basically doing everything but selling peanuts in the stands. If the Brewers close out their first World Series title since 1982, Contreras will have a strong case for Series MVP.

stories.headline: The Rays Are Sending a Former Brewer to Save Their Season in Game 3
stories.body: Tampa Bay is turning to Freddy Peralta — acquired from the Mets at the deadline and 7-0 with a 0.89 ERA over his last 10 outings — to keep the Rays' World Series hopes alive. Nothing like asking a guy to beat his old team to avoid going down 3-0.

stories.headline: Giants Bench Jameis, Hand Keys to J.J. McCarthy
stories.body: New York is turning to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback as coach John Harbaugh called it part of a broader team evaluation — which is a polite way of saying things aren't working. Jameis Winston, meanwhile, adds another stop to his tour of NFL benches.

stories.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Rumors Are Heating Up — Chiefs and Steelers Are Circling
stories.body: After back-to-back games without a single catch, the Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. is reportedly drawing trade interest from Kansas City and Pittsburgh. Jacksonville hasn't confirmed anything, but two stonkingly quiet games from a premier receiver tends to get people talking.

stories.headline: Lamar Jackson Still Out, Tyler Huntley Running Baltimore's Offense for Third Straight Week
stories.body: A high-ankle sprain has kept Lamar Jackson sidelined through Week 7, with Tyler Huntley making his third consecutive start for the Ravens. Baltimore's offense is managing, but there's a reason Lamar is the MVP and Huntley is the backup.

stories.headline: Antonelli Cruises to Win No. 9, Title Within Arm's Reach
stories.body: Kimi Antonelli dominated the United States Grand Prix at COTA, beating Leclerc by over 13 seconds to move just two points away from the world championship. The 20-year-old can wrap it up in Mexico City next weekend with a ninth-place finish or better.

stories.headline: Ferrari's Upgrade Finally Delivers, McLaren Has a Rough One
stories.body: Leclerc and Hamilton finished second and fourth in Austin, with Ferrari's latest upgrade package looking like a genuine step forward. McLaren had the opposite weekend — tyre troubles for both Norris and Piastri let Red Bull erase their gap in the constructors' standings.

stories.headline: Four Drivers, Eight Points: The Fight for Second Is Chaos
stories.body: Russell leads Hamilton by one point, Hamilton leads Verstappen by five, and Verstappen leads Leclerc by three in what is genuinely the tightest four-way battle for a runner-up spot in recent memory. Everyone below Antonelli is playing for pride and positioning with five rounds left.

stories.headline: UCF Stuns No. 2 BYU in Double OT, Chaos Reigns in Week 8
stories.body: UCF took down No. 2 BYU 39–31 in double overtime, while Cincinnati knocked off No. 8 Texas Tech and Wisconsin throttled No. 16 USC 24–7 — all in the same weekend. The AP poll is going to need a moment.

stories.headline: Arch Manning and Texas Are Quietly Becoming a Problem
stories.body: Texas beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34–27 and jumped eight spots to No. 11 in the AP poll, with Arch Manning looking every bit like the hype was warranted. Meanwhile, Utah is 7–0 after Devon Dampier ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns to erase a 10-point deficit against Houston.

stories.headline: Locksley, Doeren, Aranda All Out — Coaching Carousel Gets Ugly
stories.body: Maryland fired Mike Locksley after a 12-game Big Ten losing streak, NC State parted ways with Dave Doeren after 14 seasons, and Baylor moved on from Dave Aranda — all in the same week. Someone's about to get a very good head coaching job.

stories.headline: Luka Drops 52 and the Lakers Are Already Undefeated — Sorry, Rest of the West
stories.body: Luka Dončić torched Utah for 52 points and 10 assists, putting the Lakers at 3–0 and making himself just the third player in franchise history to hit that mark after Elgin Baylor and Jerry West. It's early, but Luka is absolutely not treating it that way.

stories.headline: Thunder Hit With Another Brutal Injury as Jalen Williams Is Stretchered Off
stories.body: Oklahoma City's Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome leg injury against the Clippers and left the court on a stretcher, with no confirmed diagnosis or timetable yet available. The Thunder just handed Cason Wallace a $139 million extension, so the roster depth is there — but losing Williams early would be a serious blow to a legitimate title contender.

stories.headline: Porzingis' Health Is Failing Again and Golden State Already Wants Out
stories.body: Kristaps Porziņģis is reportedly reconsidering his basketball future after another flare-up of his postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, and the Warriors — who gave him a two-year, $40 million extension last summer — are already shopping him in trade talks. Golden State is having a rough offseason in real time.

stories.headline: Isak Is On Fire: Liverpool Cruise Past Brighton on the Back of Three Straight Scorers
stories.body: Alexander Isak bagged his sixth Premier League goal in seven games as Liverpool put Brighton away 2-0, with Pascal Groß doing Liverpool the favor of opening the scoring himself. At this rate, Isak is becoming the most expensive good decision Liverpool ever made.

stories.headline: Pulisic and McKennie Keep the USMNT Expat Tour Rolling in Serie A
stories.body: Christian Pulisic scored as AC Milan blanked Udinese 2-0, while Weston McKennie got off the schneid with his first goal of the season in Juventus's 2-0 win over Lecce. A good weekend to be American in Italy.

stories.headline: Salah in Turkey, and Three Big Clubs Are Already Eyeing His Replacement's Replacement
stories.body: Mohamed Salah is generating buzz in Trabzonspor's corner of Turkey after his August move from Liverpool, and Liverpool have reportedly moved on to scouting 18-year-old Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl — along with Arsenal and Manchester United. Karl has one goal and one assist in nine appearances, which is apparently enough to get three giants camping outside your door.

stories.headline: Zverev Locks Up Year-End No. 1 — First German to Do It Since Becker
stories.body: Alexander Zverev will finish 2026 as world No. 1 after Carlos Alcaraz lost and Jannik Sinner shut down his season early. Boris Becker last pulled this off for Germany, which tells you everything about how long that wait was.

stories.headline: Rybakina Defends Ningbo Title, Fernandez Has No Answer
stories.body: Elena Rybakina beat Leylah Fernandez to successfully defend her Ningbo crown and pocket career title No. 15, all while remaining No. 1 in the WTA rankings ahead of Sabalenka and Andreeva. The only player to take a set off her all week was Katarzyna Kawa, who at least goes home with a career-high ranking of No. 106 as a consolation prize.

stories.headline: Musetti Ends Four-Year Title Drought, Fritz Comes Up Short Again
stories.body: Lorenzo Musetti defeated Taylor Fritz in Lyon to claim his third ATP title and first in four years. Meanwhile, Tallon Griekspoor quietly won Brussels over Jan-Lennard Struff for his fourth career trophy — a solid week for the guys who weren't headlining anything.

stories.headline: Smotherman Outlasts Power in Bermuda Marathon, Pockets $1.08M
stories.body: Austin Smotherman won the Butterfield Bermuda Championship on Monday after a three-hole sudden-death playoff against Seamus Power, both having finished 72 hours of wind-delayed golf at 16-under 197. The win vaulted Smotherman to 51st in the FedExCup standings and right on the bubble of the top-50 OWGR cutoff that earns a Masters invite — suddenly this Monday grind looks like it was worth every extra hole.

stories.headline: Sabbatini Torches the Senior Field with a Sunday 62 at the Stifel Charity Classic
stories.body: Rory Sabbatini shot a closing 62 to claim his first PGA Tour Champions title at 13-under 199, edging Darren Clarke by one shot. A 62 to earn your maiden senior-tour win is a pretty emphatic way to announce you've arrived.

stories.headline: Katsuragawa Makes It Two DP World Tour Titles with Genesis Win in South Korea
stories.body: Japan's Yuto Katsuragawa won the Genesis Championship at Woo Jeong Hills by two shots at 13-under 271, with Frederic LaCroix and Martin Couvra sharing second. Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra tied for 22nd, so the door to that title remains open with only Abu Dhabi and Dubai left on the calendar.
